A little context, right where you read.

Paper reading often sends us back and forth between an argument and its references. Hover over a citation—or focus it with Tab, then press Arrow Down—to inspect its paper without leaving this paragraph.

For example, TabPFN adapts to small tabular datasets [1]. A separate thread of work introduces attention-based sequence modelling [2]. You can rate either paper from the preview and then open its details in Lens.

References without an arXiv identifier still have a readable citation [3]. Ordinary section links, such as Figure 1, do not open the popup.

A publication DOI can identify an arXiv version even without an arXiv link: [4].

Two further tabular-model references let you try the unread-reference estimate: [5] and [6].

  2. [2] Attention Is All You Need. arXiv:1706.03762

  5. RelICL: Training-free Relational Learning with Tabular Foundation Models. arXiv:2610.01725
  6. Distillation of Tabular Foundation Models into Efficient Predictors. arXiv:2610.01435
